periods.label: Before 1750
periods.note: The old town: the castle on its sandstone rock (11th century), the English borough on the hill and the French borough by the castle, joined by the market place.
Framework knitting and lace bring people in, but the town cannot spread: its common fields ring it on three sides, so it packs in and gets a name for the worst slums in England.
The Inclosure Act of 1845 opens the common fields, and the town at last grows outwards onto them.
The borough takes in Basford, Bulwell, Radford, Sneinton and more in 1877, and becomes a city in 1897. Nottingham is an international centre of lace.
Between the wars: the new Council House (1927–1929) and the first council estates.
After the war: the Clifton estate, planned from 1950 and once the largest council estate in Europe, slum clearance, and new shopping centres.
